spec.title: Export complaints to CSV
spec.goal: Compliance teams need to export what they see. Add GET /api/complaints/export.csv that returns the complaints matching the same filters the existing complaints list endpoint accepts, as RFC 4180 CSV with a header row and a Content-Disposition attachment filename containing the date. Protect against CSV/formula injection: any cell starting with =, +, -, @, tab or carriage return must be prefixed with a single quote. Stream or bound the response so large exports do not exhaust memory (cap at 10,000 rows and say so in a response header). In the frontend Complaints page add an 'Export CSV' button that downloads the export for the current filters. Add backend tests for headers, escaping of commas/quotes/newlines, formula-injection protection, filtering and the row cap, and a frontend test for the button.
spec.constraints: Reuse the existing query/filter logic rather than duplicating it. No new dependencies. All checks must pass.

tasks.title: Implement GET /api/complaints/export.csv reusing list filters
acceptance: GET /api/complaints/export.csv returns 200 with Content-Type text/csv and a Content-Disposition attachment filename containing the current date.
The endpoint accepts the same filter query parameters as GET /api/complaints and returns the same filtered set, implemented by reusing/extracting the existing filter logic rather than duplicating it.
Output begins with a header row and each record is RFC 4180 compliant (comma separators, doubled quotes inside quoted fields, records ended with CRLF).
Any cell value starting with =, +, -, @, tab or carriage return is prefixed with a single quote before quoting.
Response is streamed or otherwise bounded and capped at 10,000 rows, with a response header (e.g. X-Export-Truncated or X-Total-Rows) indicating the cap was applied when truncated.
No new dependencies are added.

tasks.title: Add Export CSV button to Complaints page
acceptance: frontend/src/pages/Complaints.tsx renders an 'Export CSV' button.
Clicking the button navigates/triggers a download of /api/complaints/export.csv with the currently applied filters serialized as query parameters.
Button is disabled or hidden when no filters/list context is available and does not break existing page rendering.
No new dependencies are added.

tasks.title: Backend tests for CSV export headers, escaping, injection, filtering, cap
acceptance: A new test module under backend/tests/ covers: response headers (Content-Type, Content-Disposition with date) and header row.
Tests assert correct escaping of commas, double quotes and newlines inside cell values.
Tests assert formula-injection values beginning with =, +, -, @, tab, or CR are prefixed with a single quote.
Tests assert filtering matches the existing complaints list endpoint for at least one filter combination.
Tests assert the 10,000-row cap and the truncation/row-count response header using a seeded dataset larger than the cap.
Tests run green via scripts/atlas/test-backend.sh.

tasks.title: Frontend test for Export CSV button
acceptance: A test verifies the 'Export CSV' button renders on the Complaints page.
The test verifies clicking the button requests /api/complaints/export.csv with the current filter query parameters (e.g. via mocked fetch/window.location).
Test runs green under scripts/atlas/test-frontend.sh and type/lint checks pass.
